html:
SMTO-LLM-0085 — SMTO couldn't confirm your model works with it

GUID: 4a7ef1ac-eb5a-4ed1-930e-1564245c8b17
Slug: model-readiness-inconclusive
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • SMTO sent your model one short test request, but the result didn't prove everything SMTO needs works. That doesn't mean the model is broken; tasks can still run and will report their own problems.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Try a normal task with this model. This test is only advisory; real tasks still run and show their own message if something is wrong.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model to test again. A model that was still loading or busy during the first test often passes a second time.
  3. If it stays unconfirmed and tasks fail too, select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs your model service. The details show which part of the test the model didn't complete, such as answering too slowly or with the wrong value.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passed, or your tasks complete normally.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO or your model service. Don't turn off security or certificate checks to make the test pass, and don't repeat tasks that already finished just to test the model.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The one-request model check finished without proof of the required behaviour: it ran out of time or output allowance, the model returned a different tool or value than the test asked for, or another non-configuration failure occurred. This does not establish that the endpoint lacks tool support.

What this means

  • A diagnostic can finish without proof when generation is slow, its allowance is exhausted, or the model answers differently from the fixture. This does not establish that the endpoint lacks tool support. Normal task validation still applies.

Why this can happen

  • A diagnostic can finish without proof when generation is slow, its allowance is exhausted, or the model answers differently from the fixture. This does not establish that the endpoint lacks tool support. Normal task validation still applies.

How to diagnose it

  • The bounded diagnostic did not establish all required model behavior.
  • The single startup request returns the expected complete fixture tool call; normal tasks validate their own responses.

How to fix it

  • Read the check's stage and error detail in the error details or diagnostic report. If the model was slow or still loading, warm it up and rerun Check saved model; if it returned the wrong tool or value, try a real task, which validates its own responses. The result is advisory and does not block tasks; the startup check runs again only when the Server restarts.
  • Inspect the startup check details before changing provider settings. This result is advisory: normal tasks can proceed and report their own errors. A new startup check occurs only when the controller restarts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • The single startup request returns the expected complete fixture tool call; normal tasks validate their own responses.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
